title: Evaluation of a depth-2 AND circuit matches its CNF
statement: Let $cs$ be a list of normal-form OR circuits on $n$ variables, and suppose that every entry of $cs$ is an OR-clause — that is, a base clause given by a list of literals, rather than an internal OR node. Then for every assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbf_2$, evaluating the normal-form AND circuit that conjoins the circuits in $cs$ agrees with evaluating the CNF formula built from it: the value at $x$ of the AND-node over $cs$ equals the value at $x$ of the CNF whose clauses are obtained by converting each OR-clause of $cs$ into a disjunction of literals.
hypotheses_covered: cs is a list of normal-form OR circuits on n variables
every entry of cs is an OR-clause (of clause form, not a node)
x is an assignment of the n variables
replaced:
If every child $c$ of an $\texttt{NAndCircuit}.\mathrm{node}\,cs$ is an OR-clause, then for
all $x$ the circuit evaluation $(\texttt{NAndCircuit}.\mathrm{node}\,cs).\mathrm{eval}\,x$
equals the CNF evaluation $\texttt{CNF.eval}\,((\texttt{NAndCircuit}.\mathrm{node}\,cs).\mathrm{toCNF})\,x$.
